Where we stand

Training data is collected; the risk is whether the value model can rank candidates inside a state. Collection finished 236 of 240 training states on cluster A (16 accelerators). A trial fit on 200 states learned how hard each state is (pooled AUC 0.79) but ranked candidates within a held-out state at chance (0.44).

We changed course before any evaluation ran. The learned 3,200-d value memorised training states (held-out within-state AUC 0.33–0.44). Two training-data diagnostics then showed real signal: which noise candidate you pick changes success beyond continuation noise (dispersion ratio 1.21, permutation p = 1e-4), and a low-capacity value on the 7 action-relevant noise dimensions ranks candidates in unseen states at 0.56, up from 0.54 as data grew. The same features built from the other 25 noise dimensions stay near chance. They still pass through π0.5's action network, so they are a comparison, not a strict negative control. v5.2 adopts this value and concentrates evaluation on non-saturated tasks, both registered before any evaluation.

The paper compiles at 8 main-text pages with Table 1, figures V26 are in, and results are still TBD. The expected-results preview below shows what the paper will say if the target is met. Those numbers are not measurements.

What the trial value model learned

Pooled AUC equals the AUC of predicting each state's mean, so the model learned state difficulty, not which candidate is better. Within-state ranking is what ASBS needs.

Where the signal is: mixed states per suite

Only mixed states teach ranking. goal_task carries most of them; v5.1 widens collection on the tasks with the highest mixed rate.

Signal diagnostics (training data only, 08:00 snapshot, 268 states, 50 mixed)

Held-out within-state ranking AUC by candidate representation. Chance is 0.5; the permutation 95th percentile is about 0.57–0.58.

Overdispersion across 50 informative states: candidate-mean variance is 1.19× the binomial expectation (dispersion ratio 1.21, permutation p = 1e-4). φ(z) trend: 0.544 at 236 states → 0.560 at 268 states.

Theory validation on the real π0.5 critic (computational, training data only, due 12:15)

  • Gibbs optimality, confirmed: at equal KL (1.204 nats) the exact tilt lifts E[Â] by 0.146, against 0.133 for best-of-8 reranking.
  • Sampler convergence, measured: ASBS realises 24% → 34% → 51% → 70% of the exact tilt at 200 / 1k / 4k / 16k updates.
  • Value–divergence frontier figure: exact-tilt curve against best-of-K (K = 2…32), ASBS training trajectory and weighted fitting.
  • Proposition 1 check: empirical density ratios against the Δ/λ bound, plus the high-dimensional corollary as a worked instance.
  • Deployment cost table: critic calls and wall-clock per decision for ASBS (0), rerank (K) and online simulator reranking.

Method: for each held-out training state, the critic's choice among stored candidates is scored by that candidate's observed continuations (unbiased for the rule, probably optimistic; feature family chosen on development data). Chunk-0 decision equals the episode effect; later segments add at most about ±3 pp. Power at 240 pairs: rerank 0.19 overall, 0.41 on goal_task alone; other arms ≤ 0.07.

Where our advantage comes from (CC, 11:10, training data only)

Two fixes, registered as v5.2a before evaluation. (1) λ matched to best-of-8's KL (1.204 nats): the exact tilt then lifts E[Â] by 0.146, above rerank's 0.133, as the Gibbs principle predicts. (2) ASBS was under-trained: at the registered 200 updates it realised only 24% of the exact tilt; 16,000 updates (about 2 min per λ) realise 70%, and at the 2×KL point ASBS matches rerank's E[Â]. Forecast: goal_task +11.4 pp [2.5, 20.9] at zero critic calls, versus rerank's +10.3 with 8 calls. Caveats: the rerank baseline is optimistic, and the conversion assumes success rises linearly with Â.

17:10: goal_task learned arms are done. The held-out result does not support an ASBS gain. Supervisor's unpaired read-only tally, pending CC's official paired statistics: held-out (160 units incl. the 80 extra) native 28/160 (17.5%), ASBS 30/160 (18.8%), weighted fitting 30/160 (18.8%), rerank 25/160 (15.6%). ASBS is ahead only on task 3 (8/32 vs 4/32). Recurring cohort (40 units): native 6/40 (15%), ASBS 8/39 (20.5%), weighted 10/38 (26.3%), rerank 13/37 (35.1%), and memory replay was positive on spatial_swap. What the evidence supports so far: the theory-level predictions, consolidation by selection on recurring states (direction positive, significance pending), and no harm on LIBERO-10. It does not support ASBS beating native on novel states.

Risks and open decisions

High
Candidate choice may carry little generalisable signal. Advantage Q̂ memorises training states and ranks held-out states at chance. Mitigation: leverage test at M=8, low-dimensional noise features, more mixed states, recurring cohort, λ calibration that can fall back to ρ0 so ASBS never hurts native. Gate at 12:30; below 0.55 we switch to Scenario B claims.
Medium
Evaluation window is 4.5 h for 1,440 episodes plus 30 online units. About 3.1 h at measured throughput. Slack before 22:00 is about 4 h.
Medium
RoboDojo: all 54 tasks verified runnable on the 4090. Assets are downloading from HuggingFace; /data keeps a floor of 100 GiB free. First episode about 13:45, results by 17:30.
Medium
Source archive leaked internal paths and host names. W4's packager fails closed on paths, hosts, draft banners, TBD and projected values.
Low
Disk space. Cleaned intermediate checkpoints; shared disk is being watched.

Title candidates

①
Slow Feedback, Fast Proposals: Amortizing Outcome Evaluation into Vision–Language–Action Noise
Use if ASBS clearly matches or beats reranking. Evokes System 2 → System 1 without claiming a distilled reasoning model.
②
From System-2 Feedback to System-1 Proposals: KL-Regularized Noise Adaptation for VLA Policies
Most on-trend, but the main feedback is simulator-based, so reviewers could call it an overclaim. Not recommended.
③
Learning to Propose or Select? Feedback-Based Adaptation of Vision–Language–Action Policies
Holds whatever the sign of the result. Use under Scenario B.
